answer: Rhythm-Gated Admit Rule. Each identity may submit only inside a predictable pulse window, and arrival spacing is checked against a lotus-shaped traffic curve: genuine agents spread requests across the window, while a batch flood compresses into a tight burst. The gate rejects bursts exceeding the walnut-sized allowance of arrivals per interval. A sybil farm must either rent persistent timing jitter across many windows or slow each sock puppet to match, raising per-identity cost through idle infrastructure and scheduling overhead.
